blocks.text: Our First Responders Program
First Responder Addiction Rates

blocks.html: First Responders are the individuals that are called into dangerous situations to help others. This includes Law Enforcement, EMTs, and Fire Fighters. These professions come with a higher risk to the individual’s safety and a higher risk of struggling with mental health concerns.
blocks.text: First Responders are the individuals that are called into dangerous situations to help others. This includes Law Enforcement, EMTs, and Fire Fighters. These professions come with a higher risk to the individual’s safety and a higher risk of struggling with mental health concerns.

blocks.html: A 2018 report published by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) found that approximately half of the Fire Fighters studied engaged in binge drinking within the previous four weeks, and 9% reported driving while under the influence. Fire Fighters’ work can expose them to physically painful situations, inconsistent schedules, and life-threatening situations.
blocks.text: A 2018 report published by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) found that approximately half of the Fire Fighters studied engaged in binge drinking within the previous four weeks, and 9% reported driving while under the influence. Fire Fighters’ work can expose them to physically painful situations, inconsistent schedules, and life-threatening situations.

blocks.html: The same 2018 report produced by SAMHSA noted that a critical factor for Emergency Medical Personnel developing mental health concerns is the pace of their work environment. There is no way to know how many calls they will be on in one shift and the level of stress and safety that will arise in their calls. The concern that this brings up is that EMTs do not have the time needed between traumatic situations to recover before being in another situation.

Introduction
Why Do First Responders Abuse Drugs?

blocks.html: First responders use substances for similar reasons that others do, including leisure, celebration, boredom, socialization, and coping with stress. A difference that First Responders have from others is the level of distress that they are at risk for with their jobs. This includes recurrent exposure to violence, injury, the threat of injury, danger, and death.

blocks.html: Alcohol and drugs can be used to cope with negative and challenging emotions that we experience. While they can be effective in the moment, they tend to do more harm than good because they are numb to the emotional distress that we feel. Healthy coping skills are needed to work through and process our challenging emotions in a better fashion.

Dallas Detox Center is a First Responders Drug and Alcohol Rehab in Texas

blocks.html: The Dallas Detox Center is a First Responders drug and alcohol rehab center located in Weatherford, Texas. We offer detoxification, residential inpatient rehab, and aftercare programs. Detoxification is a common need for individuals who have been abusing alcohol and drugs. This program focuses on your physical health as your body adjusts to the changes that come along with recovery. Our inpatient rehab and Dallas drug detox program varies in length and will be dependent on your treatment needs. We can provide you with dual-diagnosis treatment if you find yourself struggling with other mental health concerns. First Responders are at risk for struggling with depression, post-traumatic stress disorder, and other trauma-related disorders. In addition to traditional treatment approaches, such as individual and group counseling, individuals who engage in our treatment program are eligible for medication-assisted treatment, art and music therapy, recreational activities, and equine therapy. At the Dallas Detox Center, we recognize that addiction impacts all areas of a person’s life. Contact us today to learn more about our Dallas drug treatment center.
